title: MICRO ARCADE
_comment: The kiosk library. Copy to games.json and edit; games.json is gitignored,
so a personal library stays out of the repository. Bundles are never
committed either.
CONTROL BUDGET: a tilt sensor and one button, and the button is the
screen itself -- pressing it hides the picture. Tilt carries anything
continuous; the button is for taps. Long press is reserved by the kiosk
for 'back to the menu' and cannot be bound. Nothing needing a held
button, a mouse, or typing.
SELECT AND PLAY: the cabinet cannot read a DOS menu -- the text is
unreadable at 128x128 and there is no pointer -- so boot_keys has to
carry a title all the way from the launcher into gameplay: sound-card
prompt, title screens, pilot name, difficulty, briefing, the lot. Every
entry below was auditioned by scripting those keys, then holding a
movement key and checking that the picture answered it. A title that
could not be driven into gameplay is not in this file.
BUNDLES: `exodos` names the entry in an eXoDOS collection. Build one with
python server/jsdos/from-exodos.py "Heretic (1994)"
which writes the .jsdos named in `bundle` next to the js-dos backend, or
build every title in this file at once with
python server/jsdos/build-library.py
BOOT KEYS: each step waits that many milliseconds after the previous one,
then taps a key. To work out a sequence for a new title, run
python server/jsdos/audition.py "Some Game (1993)"
which writes a filmstrip of what it saw next to the backend: read the
menu it stalled on, add the keys that answer it, and run it again.
Key names: service/microstream/keys.py. Roles: left right up down fire
double use run start menu.
CATALOGUES: the menu lists entries whose "catalog" includes "play"; the
demo reel runs entries that include "demo". Leave it out for both. The
reel boots real games live, controls working; "demo_keys" replaces
boot_keys there and "demo_s" overrides how long a title stays up.
SETTINGS: kiosk.double_click and reel.double_click are "game" (the game
gets it) or "next" (skip to the next title). reel.advance_s moves the
reel on by itself, 0 to wait for a double click. reel.idle_s starts the
reel from an untouched menu, 0 never. run.py --reel starts in the reel.
EXODOS: a DOS title with no bundle runs in place from the collection at
exodos.root (or EXODOS_ROOT, or run.py --exodos-root): nothing copied.
prefer "in_place" skips bundles even when they exist. max_mb skips zips
too big to run, since one takes about five times its size in memory.
AUTOPILOT: in the reel, a title nobody is holding plays itself once its
boot keys are done: reel.autopilot holds, taps and weaves between roles
(forward and fire by default). A title's "demo_input" overrides it, or
false leaves it alone. Pressing or tilting takes over at once; the
autopilot resumes after 6 idle seconds.

games.title: Skyrim
games.verified: a recording, not the game: plays in real time and loops
games.note: Not emulated and not interactive. A video, streamed through the same rectangle pipeline as every game, because a dumb terminal cannot tell the difference. Supply your own file in kiosk/media/; it is gitignored and never goes in the repository.

games.title: Second Reality
games.verified: slot only: appears once the video file is in kiosk/media/
games.note: Future Crew, 1993. Recorded rather than emulated; drop a capture of it at kiosk/media/second_reality.mp4 and it joins the demo reel.

games.title: Dragon's Lair
games.verified: starts a game (score and lives screen, drawbridge scene); timing windows with tilt not yet tried on the device
games.note: The laserdisc game, in ReadySoft's PC version. Every scene is a quick-time event: lean the way Dirk has to go, tap to swing the sword. Left alone it plays its own attract demo, which is what the reel shows.

games.title: Singe's Castle
games.exodos: Dragon's Lair - Escape from Singe's Castle (1991)
games.verified: starts a game (Dirk in the castle); timing with tilt not yet tried
games.note: Dragon's Lair's sequel scenes. ReadySoft's setup screen wants letters: V for VGA, N for no sound, N for no joystick, N for no install.

games.title: Dragon's Lair II
games.verified: starts a game (score and lives screen, tavern scene); timing with tilt not yet tried
games.note: Time Warp reads the numeric keypad: numpad 0 starts and swings, 8/2/4/6 move. The tilt maps to those, so the cabinet does not care.

games.title: Space Ace
games.verified: starts a game (Ace running, then game over); timing with tilt not yet tried
games.note: Its 'Press Fire Button to Start' ignores Space, Enter, Ctrl and Alt: the keyboard fire button is numpad 0. The reel skips the press and shows the attract loop instead.

games.title: Space Ace II
games.verified: intro loop plays; the game itself stops at a copy-protection prompt
games.note: Demo reel only: starting a game asks for a protection code from the manual. The intro before that is all cinema.

games.title: Guy Spy
games.exodos: Guy Spy and the Crystals of Armageddon (1992)
games.verified: title and credits loop; starting a game not tried yet
games.note: A ReadySoft CD title. Its disc image mounts as D:, which needed the bundler to match the image's file-name case. Answers VGA, no sound, no joystick.

games.title: Mad Dog McCree
games.verified: attract sequence plays: title, saloon, shootout
games.note: Full-motion video western on a CD image. It wants a light gun, so it lives in the demo reel, where its attract sequence runs by itself.

games.title: Brain Dead 13
games.verified: animated intro plays
games.note: ReadySoft's animated cartoon adventure, 456 MB of CD, run in place from eXoDOS.

games.title: Crime Patrol
games.verified: attract sequence plays
games.note: American Laser Games full-motion video on a CD image, run in place from eXoDOS. It wants a light gun, so it lives in the demo reel, where its attract sequence runs by itself.

games.title: Drug Wars
games.verified: attract sequence plays
games.note: American Laser Games full-motion video on a CD image, run in place from eXoDOS. It wants a light gun, so it lives in the demo reel, where its attract sequence runs by itself.

games.title: Mad Dog II
games.exodos: Mad Dog II - The Lost Gold (1994)
games.verified: attract sequence plays
games.note: American Laser Games full-motion video on a CD image, run in place from eXoDOS. It wants a light gun, so it lives in the demo reel, where its attract sequence runs by itself.

games.title: Who Shot Johnny Rock
games.verified: attract sequence plays
games.note: American Laser Games full-motion video on a CD image, run in place from eXoDOS. It wants a light gun, so it lives in the demo reel, where its attract sequence runs by itself.

games.title: Space Pirates
games.verified: attract sequence plays
games.note: American Laser Games full-motion video on a CD image, run in place from eXoDOS. It wants a light gun, so it lives in the demo reel, where its attract sequence runs by itself.

games.title: Los Justicieros
games.verified: intro and attract scenes play
games.note: Spanish light-gun western in full-motion video, on a CD image run in place.

games.title: Rebel Assault
games.verified: intro plays
games.note: LucasArts' CD-ROM showpiece: logo, X-wings, Vader, all from a 295 MB disc image run in place.

games.title: Fort Boyard
games.verified: intro plays, then a still menu
games.note: Its intro, then its main menu, which needs a mouse. A short turn in the reel.

games.title: Stunts
games.verified: in-game: car on the track, answers the throttle
games.note: Polygonal 3D driving with a track editor, in 1990. Lean to steer, lean forward to accelerate -- tilt fits this better than a keyboard ever did.

games.title: Test Drive III
games.verified: in-game: driving, scenery scrolling past
games.note: Full 3D open roads and a dashboard drawn in loving detail. That dashboard alone is more pixels than the ESP32 has memory for.

games.title: Stunt Driver
games.verified: in-game: on the course under throttle
games.note: Spectrum HoloByte's stunt course: loops, jumps and a chase camera. Steering and throttle are the whole game.

games.title: Indianapolis 500
games.verified: in-game: out of the pits, cockpit view
games.note: Papyrus's simulation, the start of the lineage that ends at iRacing. It opens in an attract loop that says PRESS ESCAPE TO DRIVE, and the menu behind it already sits on PRACTICE -- so the cabinet never reads a menu.

games.title: SkyRoads
games.verified: in-game: on the track and accelerating
games.note: Drive and jump along a ribbon of road in space. Steer with tilt, jump with a tap, nothing held -- the closest thing to a native fit for this cabinet, and the most legible title in the library at 128x128.

games.title: F-15 Strike Eagle II
games.verified: in-game: airborne, HUD live, answers pitch
games.note: MicroProse's flight sim, with a full instrument panel and a 3D world underneath it. Tilt is the stick, which is what a stick wants to be.

games.title: Wolfenstein 3D
games.verified: in-game: walking a corridor, doors opening
games.note: The one that invented the genre. Tilt turns, a tap fires, a double tap opens doors.

games.title: Blake Stone
games.verified: in-game: corridor, enemy met, taking damage
games.note: The Wolfenstein engine with a science-fiction skin, informants to talk to and a floor map. Walks and shoots on the same three controls.

games.title: Catacomb 3-D
games.verified: in-game: dungeon corridor, status bar live
games.note: Carmack's first texture-mapped first-person engine, months before Wolfenstein. Throwing fireballs down a dungeon corridor in 1992.

games.title: Heretic
games.verified: in-game: walking a castle, full HUD
games.note: The DOOM engine with look-up, flight and an inventory. Bigger and prettier than anything that fits in ESP32 flash, on a 0.85in screen.

games.title: Rise of the Triad
games.exodos: Rise of the Triad - The Hunt Begins (Deluxe Edition) (1995)
games.verified: in-game: outdoors, weapon drawn, moving
games.note: Wolfenstein's engine pushed past breaking point: jump pads, tilting floors and absurd weapons.

games.title: Major Stryker
games.verified: in-game: flying the level, firing
games.note: Apogee's horizontal shooter: parallax starfields and a screen full of sprites. Tilt flies, the button shoots.

games.title: Tyrian
games.verified: in-game: level scrolling, ship under control
games.note: One of the best-looking shooters on DOS. Its Game Menu opens on the Data reader, so the sequence backs out of that and walks down to Play Next Level -- exactly the select-and-play the cabinet needs.

games.title: Duke Nukem
games.verified: in-game: running and jumping through the level
games.note: Before the third dimension: EGA, sixteen colours, and a jump that lands where you meant it to. Tap jumps, double tap shoots.

games.title: Commander Keen 4
games.exodos: Commander Keen 4 - Secret of the Oracle (1991)
games.verified: in-game: walking the world map
games.note: Smooth-scrolling EGA platforming that PCs were not supposed to manage, plus a world map to wander. Tap jumps, double tap pogos.

games.title: Cosmo's Cosmic Adventure
games.verified: in-game: walking the level, scenery scrolling
games.note: Cosmo sticks to walls with his suction-cup hands. One button is the whole game, which is precisely this cabinet's budget.

games.title: Jill of the Jungle
games.verified: in-game: Jill walking the level
games.note: Epic's first platformer, and the one that put them on the map. Runs, jumps and throws knives on three controls.

games.title: Crystal Caves
games.verified: in-game: in the cave, moving
games.note: Mine crystals, avoid everything else. Compact, readable and fast, which matters a lot at 128x128.

games.title: Bio Menace
games.verified: in-game: running the level
games.note: Apogee's answer to the console run-and-guns, on the Keen engine with a gun bolted on.

games.title: Hocus Pocus
games.verified: in-game: moving through the level
games.note: A wizard, a lot of VGA colour, and levels built out of floating brick. One of the better-looking shareware platformers.

games.title: Prehistorik 2
games.verified: in-game: walking the level, club in hand
games.note: Titus at their most charming: a caveman with a club, hand-drawn and hugely colourful.

games.title: Prince of Persia
games.verified: in-game: in the dungeon, under control
games.note: Rotoscoped animation in 1990: every step, jump and stumble traced from film. Still the most convincing movement of its decade.

games.title: DOOM
games.note: Native doomgeneric, and the only profile that knows its game's state: the button means ENTER in menus, USE when dead, FIRE in play.

games.title: Digger
games.note: Windmill Software released it as freeware in 1998, and js-dos hosts it. Four directions and one button is the entire game, so it is the safest thing here and the one that proves the pipeline.
